la:verb:moneo.html:
mŏnĕo, ŭi, ĭtum, 2 (
inf. pres. pass. monerier, ; perf. subj. moneris pro monueris, Pac. ap. ; cf. Trag. Rel. p. 66 Rib.; likewise: di monerint meliora, Pac. ap. Non. l. l. p. 74 Rib.), v. a.
causative from the root men; whence memini, q. v., mens, mentio; lit. to cause to think
.
Lit., to remind, put in mind of, bring to one's recollection; to admonish, advise, warn, instruct, teach (syn.: hortor, suadeo, doceo): bene mones; tute ipse cunctas, Enn. ap. (Com. v. 3 Vahl.): ea (auctoritas) adhibeatur ad monendum non modo aperte, sed etiam acriter,: melius nos Zenonis praecepta monent,.—
Aliquem de re: oro, ut Terentiam moneatis de testamento,; .—
Aliquem aliquid: Fabius ea me ex tuis mandatis monuit,: id ipsum, quod me mones,: sed eos hoc moneo, desinant furere,: vos quo pauca monerem advocavi,; .— Hence also in pass., moneri aliquid: ut moneatur semper servos homo officium suam,: nec ea, quae ab eā (naturā) monemur, audimus,; cf. infra. ξ.—
Aliquem alicujus rei (post-Aug., and only in Tac.; cf.: admoneo, commonefacio): Caecina milites temporis ac necessitatis monet, Nipperd. ad loc.: Plancinam Augusta monuit Agrippinam insectandi,.— (ε) With ut, ne, or the simple subj.: monere te atque hortari, ut in rem publicam incumberes,: monet ut suspiciones vitet,: moneo, praedico, ante denuntio, abstineant, manus : moneo obtestorque ut, etc.,; ; : vos, ne amittatis, etc.,: Macedonas monebat, ne multitudine hostium ... moverentur,: quamquam edicto monuisset ne quis quietem ejus interrumperet,—(ξ) With an object- or rel.-clause: (Caesar) monuit ejus diei victoriam in earum cohortium virtute constare,: moneret rationem frumenti esse habendam,: Cerealis propinquos monebat fortunam belli mutare, etc.,: Arminius colligi suos et propinquare silvis monitos vertit,: ultro struebantur qui monerent perfugere ad Germaniae exercitus,fin.: Radamistum obpugnationem celerare,; 13, 37; 16, 11; : si te unum illud monuerimus, artem sine assiduitate dicendi non multum juvare,: moneo, quid facto opus sit,: res monet cavere, consultare,: alio properare tempus monet,.—Pass.: cum Nicanorem insidiari Piraeo a Dercillo moneretur,.—
Of inanim. and abstr. subjects: res ipsa monebat tempus esse,: (sol) caecos instare tumultus Saepe monet,: immortalia ne speres, monet annus,: natura monet festinare,: ut monet ira,: ratio ipsa monet amicitias comparare,.—
Transf. (mostly poet. and in post-Aug. prose).
Without the accessory notion of reminding or admonishing, in gen., to teach, instruct, tell, inform, point out; also, to announce, predict, foretell: tu vatem, tu diva, mone,instruct thy bard,: velut divinitus mente monitā,: hoc moneas precor,: amici somnio monitus,: reddebant parvuli, quae monebantur,what they were taught,: vates Helenus cum multa horrenda moneret,announced, foretold,; cf.: ante sinistra cavā monuisset ab ilice cornix, etc.,: quid augurales alites vel cantus monerent,: recte monemur, causas non utique ab ultimo esse repetendas,.—
To punish, chastise (only in Tacitus): puerili verbere moneri,.

la:noun:mons.html:
mons, tis (archaic abl. montei, Enn. ap. ; cf. Ann. v. 420 Vahl.), m.
etym. dub., perh. from the root min, whence also, emineo, mentum, minari; cf. minae; lit. a projecting body; hence
,
a mountain, mount.
Lit.: montium altitudines,: altissimi,: avii,: inaccessi,: lapidosi,.—Prov.: parturiunt montes, nascetur ridiculus mus, said where much is promised but little performed,.—
Transf.
A mountain, i. e. a (heaped-up, towering) mass, a heap, quantity: argenti montes,: montes mali ardentes,; : ita mali maeroris montem maxumum conspicatus sum,: mons in Tusculani monte,i. e. a lofty, splendid building near Tusculum,: aquae,: armorum,.—Of a wagon-load of stones: eversum fudit super agmina montem,; .—Prov.: montes auri polliceri,to promise mountains of gold, to make great promises,; so, maria montesque polliceri,: magnos montes promittere,.—
A mountain-rock, rock in gen. (poet.): fertur in abruptum magno mons improbus actu,: Graii,Greek marble,.—
Mountain-beasts, wild beasts (late poet.): consumant totos spectacula montes,.

moneta

la:noun:monumentum.html:
mŏnŭmentum (mŏnĭm-), i, n. [moneo),
that which preserves the remembrance of any thing, a memorial, a monument; esp. of buildings, statues, galleries, tombs erected to perpetuate the remembrance of a person or thing; cf. Paul. ex Müll.
Lit. (class.): statuam dare auream Solidam faciundam, quae siet factis monumentum suis,: monimenti causā,: monumento ut esset,: vitiorum,: Marcelli et Africani,, § 11: in Mamertino solo foederato atque pacato monumentum istius, crudelitatis constitutum est,, § 26: ego, quae monumenti ratio sit, nomine ipso admoneor, ad memoriam magis spectare debet posteritatis, quam ad praesentis temporis gratiam, ap. : placet mihi, legionis Martiae militibus monumentum fieri quam amplissimum,; plur. excellent: quod in monumentis majorum suorum sit interfectus (Clodius),i. e. on the Via Appia,; : pecunias monumentaque, quae ex fano Herculis collata erant,memorials, votive offerings, images,: monimenta, quae in sepulcris: et ideo secundum viam, quo praetereuntes admoneant, et se fuisse, et illos esse mortales, Müll.: regis,: Marii,the temple built by him,; of the temple of Castor,: senatūs,the house of Cicero, built by order of the Senate,.—
In partic.
A sepulchral monument, a sepulchre, tomb (syn.: sepulcrum, tumulus; class.): marmoreum, Serv. ap. : sepulcri,; and without sepulcri: sepultus est in monumento avunculi sui,family tomb, sepulchre,.—
Of written works, monuments, or records: exegi monumentum aere perennius,: monumenta rerum gestarum, books of history, chronicles, Cic. de Or. 1, 46, 201: annalium,the monuments of history,: commendare aliquid monumentis,memoirs,: liber monumenti,.—
Transf., a remembrancer, a mark, token, or means of recognition, : vos monimentis commonefaciam bubulis,.—
Trop.: at illa laus est, magno in genere ... liberos hominem educare, generi monumentum et sibi,: monumentum laudis,a memorial,: clementiae,: furtorum,: amoris,.

la:verb:monstro.gloss: to show, point out, indicate, demonstrate
senses: to show, point out, indicate, demonstrate
la:verb:monstro.html:
monstro, āvi, ātum, (archaic mostro; v. Brix ad ), 1, v. a.
like monstrum, from moneo
,
to show, point out, to indicate, intimate, inform, advise, teach, instruct, tell any thing (in class. prose very rare, and only in the lit. signif.; in Cic. only a few times; in Cæs. and Sall. not at all; syn.: indico, significo, ostendo, exhibeo).
In gen.: qui erranti comiter monstrat viam, Enn. ap. (Trag. v. 387 Vahl.); cf.: qui sibi semitam non sapiunt, alteri monstrant viam, id. ap. (Trag. v. 358 Vahl.): iter,: palmam,: digito,; : monstra quod bibam,; : tu ... si quid librari ... non intellegent, monstrabis, i. e. dices,: res gestae ... Quo scribi possent numero, monstravit Homerus,: inulas ego primus amaras Monstravi incoquere,: monstrate mearum Vidistis si quam hic errantem forte sororum,: cujus prudentia monstrat Summos posse viros ... nasci, etc.,.—Pass.: quod monstror digito praetereuntium,.— Impers. pass.: si voles advortere animum, comiter monstrabitur, Enn. ap. Müll. (Trag. v. 386 Vahl.).—
In partic.
To ordain, institute, appoint (poet.): monstratas excitat aras,appointed,: piacula,: ignis,.—
To indict, impeach for a crime, to denounce, accuse, inform against (post-Aug.): alii ab amicis monstrabantur,were pointed out, informed against,: Nerone Scribonios fratres ... ad exitium,.—
To advise a person in any manner, or to do any thing: alicui bene,: non periclumst ne quid recte monstres,: conferre manum pudor iraque monstrat,advise, urge,.—Hence, monstrātus, a, um, P. a., conspicuous, distinguished, remarkable (Tacitean): et hostibus simul suisque monstrati,: propinquitate Galbae monstratus,.

senses: a divine omen indicating misfortune, an evil omen, portent
a monster, monstrosity, whether in size or character
a thing that evokes fear and wonder
la:noun:monstrum.html:
monstrum, i, n.
moneo
.
Orig. belonging to relig. lang., a divine omen indicating misfortune, an evil omen, portent (syn.: ostentum, prodigium, portentum): quia ostendunt, portendunt, monstrant, praedicunt, ostenta, portenta, monstra, prodigia dicuntur,; cf.: monstrum dictum velut monestrum, quod moneat aliquid futurum; prodigium velut praedicium, quod praedicat; portentum quod portendat; ostentum, quod ostendat, Paul. ex and 138 Müll.; cf. : hic est nullum (dubium) quin monstrum siet, Enn. ap. (Trag. v. 326 Vahl.): monstra deūm,; cf. .—
Transf., a monster, monstrosity (whether a living being or an inanimate thing).
Ofliving beings: monstrum hominis,you monster of a man,: monstrum advenit,: horrendum, of Polyphemus,.—Also with respect to character: en monstrum mulieris,that monster of a woman,: nulla jam pernicies a monstro illo atque prodigio comparabitur,: fatale, of Cleopatra,: tune etiam, immanissimum ac foedissimum monstrum ausus es?: hominum,monsters of men,.—Of beasts: succinctam latrantibus inguina monstris, i. e. canibus,: quae plurima terrae monstra ferunt,.—
Of inanim. things, of the sea, : infelix, of the Trojan horse,.—Of the ship Argo, : non mihi jam furtum, sed monstrum ac prodigium videbatur,: monstra narrare, dicere, to relate wonders, prodigies, marvels: mera monstra narrabat,: dicere,: ac portenta loqui,: totaque jam sparsis exarserat insula monstris,: in vitā suā fecit monstra,he did wonderful things,; Sap. 19, 8.

Leg. Coll. 15, 2, 6.

la:noun:moneta.html:
Mŏnēta, ae (archaic
gen. Monetas, Liv. Andron. ap. P.), f.
moneo

The mother of the Muses, a transl. of the Gr. Μνημοσύνη: Μνημοσύνη Moneta, Gloss. Philox.; cf. ; Hyg. Fab. praef.: filia Monetas, Liv. Andron. ap. P.—
A surname of Juno, in whose temple at Rome money was coined: cum terrae motus factus esset, Ut sue plena procuratio fieret, vocem ab aede Junonis ex arce exstitisse; quocirca Junonem illam appellatam Monetam,; cf. ; ; ; ; ; : ubi nunc aedes atque officina Monetae est,.—
Transf.
The place for coining money, the mint: ad Philotimum scripsi de viatico, sive a moneta, sive ab Oppiis, i. e. taken from the mint or borrowed from the Oppian usurers, ; : monetae officinator,master of the mint,: monetae aequator,.—
Coined money, coin, money (poet. and in post-Aug. prose): victaque concedit prisca moneta novae,: nigrae, i. e. aereae,; : falsam monetam percussisse,: probata,.—
A stamp or die for coining money: a novā monetā,of a new stamp,.—Hence, trop.: communi feriat carmen triviale moneta,of the common stamp, in ordinary style,: jam tempus est quaedam ex nostrā, ut ita dicam, monetā proferri,: nomina Graeca Latinā monetā percussa,of the Latin stamp,.

mŏnogrammus or -os, -on, adj., = μονόγραμμος, lit. of pictures,
